definitions.explanation: An attitude or stance that refuses to make concessions. Typically describes a negotiating position, political stance, or response that is forceful and unbending.

examples.japanese: {強硬|きょうこう}な{姿勢|しせい}を{崩|くず}さない。
examples.english: Maintain a hardline stance without wavering.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{強硬|きょうこう}{手段|しゅだん}に{出|で}る{構|かま}えだ。
examples.english: The government is prepared to resort to forceful measures.

examples.japanese: {労働組合|ろうどうくみあい}は{賃上|ちんあ}げを{求|もと}めて{強硬|きょうこう}に{交渉|こうしょう}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: The labor union continued to negotiate firmly in demanding a pay raise.

notes:
USAGE:
Common in political and diplomatic reporting. Can be used as a na-adjective ({強硬|きょうこう}な〜) or as an adverb with に ({強硬|きょうこう}に). Also appears as the first element in compounds ({強硬|きょうこう}{派|は}, {強硬|きょうこう}{路線|ろせん}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {強硬|きょうこう}な{姿勢|しせい}: hardline stance
- {強硬|きょうこう}{派|は}: hardliners, hawks
- {強硬|きょうこう}{手段|しゅだん}: forceful measures
- {強硬|きょうこう}{路線|ろせん}: hardline policy
- {強硬|きょうこう}に{反対|はんたい}する: to firmly oppose
